tagline: Write a poker bot. Submit it. Best bot wins.
intro: Today you write a Python bot that plays heads-up no-limit Texas Hold'em. Your bot only decides what to do each turn; the arena deals the cards and enforces the rules.

When hacking ends you pack your bot into one .pkl file and upload it in the submission form. There is one round: every submitted bot plays every other bot, each pairing over many deals with the seats swapped so card luck mostly cancels. The bot with the best score is the champion.

timeline.title: Hacking starts
timeline.detail: Set up, write your bot and test it against the built-in opponents. Pack it with arena pack as soon as it works, so you know the process before the deadline.

timeline.title: Submission deadline
timeline.detail: Upload your .pkl in the submission form. The last working file you upload before 18:00 is the one that plays.

timeline.title: The round
timeline.detail: Every bot plays every other bot. Nothing is shown until the round is finished, then the results and the champion appear on this site.

rules: One bot per team, packed with arena pack and uploaded as a .pkl file.
Every move has a time limit of 1 second. A crash, a timeout or an illegal move is a fault: a safe move is played, and after 20 faults your bot folds for the rest of that match.
Load data and models in your bot's __init__; files on disk are not available when the arena plays your bot.
Do not attack the arena or other teams' bots, do not use the network, and do not read files outside your bot.
contact: Stuck? Find an organiser in the room. Run python -m arena validate bots/myteam to see why your bot is failing.
